description: Kindle Paperwhite 4 (10th generation, i.MX6SLL, device tree) on stock firmware 5.18.1.1.1: the stock kernel the handoff module loads into, and the physical plan of the jump. DRAFT: not run on a device
supported_zh: Kindle Paperwhite 4（第 10 代，2018 年款），固件 5.18.1.1.1
compatible_why: a device-tree boot has no machine number (__machine_arch_type is ~0); the SoC compatible is what the stock tree's root node and the next kernel's DT_MACHINE_START both name
identity_limit_why: 2G/2G: PAGE_OFFSET == PHYS_OFFSET == 0x80000000, so the kernel's lowmem is one to one up to the end of the 512 MiB of RAM; the private table clears only the user half below the module area (0x7f000000) and copies the rest (handoff/private-table.h)
cmdline_base: consoleblank=0 uart_at_4m quiet secure_cpu=1 androidboot.secure_cpu=1 androidboot.prod=1 androidboot.unlocked_kernel=false panic=5 softlockup_panic=1 hung_task_panic=1 nofalcon
cmdline_base_why: The stock command line without root=, rootwait and console= (dd_fdt in boot/devicedata requires exactly that prefix). No serial console: the first handoff (2026-11-23) stopped at 0.26 s in the 4.1 imx console write, which waits for USR2_TXDC with interrupts off, and the stock suspend had left UART1's clock gated; the stock watchdog reset the board minutes later. The log goes to the Lab126 buffer at 0x9be00000 either way. panic=5, softlockup_panic and hung_task_panic turn a hang the kernel can see into a reboot it does itself, which keeps that log; initcall_debug was on for Jumps 2-10 (the second handoff's log stopped after the serial ports with nothing to name the driver it hung in) and is off since Android starts (Jump 11), whose log it would crowd out of the 256 KB buffer; nofalcon: the next kernel leaves the Falcon storage BIOS alone (the stock kernel set it up; a second initialisation hung) and drives the eMMC with sdhci-esdhc-imx (kernel patch 0012)
midr_why: Cortex-A9 r4p1, from the device's /proc/cpuinfo (implementer 0x41, variant 0x4, part 0xc09, revision 1)
prrr_nmrr_why: measured by the first device PROBE (2026-11-23): PRRR 0x000a81a8, NMRR 0x40e040e0, TTBR0 walk attributes 0x59, ACTLR 0xe (SMP bit clear): the SMP_ON_UP kernel found itself on one core and took the UP values, the same as PW3's
forbidden_why: destinations stay in the low 128 MiB; above it are the EPDC reservation (0x9b000000, 3 MiB), the printk buffer (0x9be00000) and the Falcon BIOS (0x9ffc0000-0x9fff0000), which the next kernel needs as the stock one left them
stock_functions_source: sizes: distance to the next text symbol in the device's /proc/kallsyms (80069564, 800229b8, 80021cec); hashes: of those bytes in the device's own memory (readom-probe2 /dev/mem dumps, 2026-11-23), not of a rebuild, whose code differs. The dump's outer_cache has flush_all = 800229b8 and disable = 80021cec and no write_sec, so the L2 is driven from the secure world directly; l2c310_disable tail-calls l2c_disable (800219c4), which is not pinned
entry_why: as the PW3 profile's, for the release entry: the PW4 PID 1 loads the v2 EPDC driver and the Goodix touch driver (device/amazon/pw4/porting/handoff.md, Jump 10), panic=5 is already in cmdline_base, and the device archive owns lib/ (lib/firmware/imx/epdc/epdc_ED060KC4.fw, which the EPDC driver asks for) as well as firmware/. None of the development switches of porting/pack-initramfs.py (pw4_lockup, a TCP shell, adb keys, boot properties) is in a release entry. The kernel release is passed to pw4-handoff-init, which loads the drivers only under the kernel they were built for
stock_files_why: as the PW3 profile's. Read on the owner's PW4, 5.18.1.1.1, on 2026-11-26 (stat -c %s and sha256sum over SSH): all four are regular files; /sbin/init and /etc/upstart/init.sh are the same 1247-byte script, which runs /sbin/init.exe as on the PW3
entry_data_why: data_format and data_bytes: the PW4's own data image, 2 GiB (device/amazon/pw4/BoardConfig.mk, the owner's decision of 2026-11-26), numbered apart from the PW3's format 1 -- 41, the PW4's first -- so that a manifest says which model's data it means. Format numbers only meet within one model (a Kindle of another model stops at E101 before its data is looked at); the number is distinct anyway, because it costs nothing, and a payload built with the other model's is then refused by build_launcher.py rather than installed
